recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No source follow-up is needed in FHIR core unless PA later reopens the Appointment/Encounter status boundary decision.
issue_request: FHIR-18827 asked to add discontinued to Appointment.status. It was Published with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution directing the change to Encounter.status instead, with Encounter.discontinued mapping to canonical abandoned and Encounter.cancelled remapped to canonical failed.
initial_application: Commit 6ac385ea8e5d79f2d56d5ff0c0f431d45374cddb explicitly applied FHIR-18827 by adding discontinued to Encounter status sources and updating the status-code matrix. Despite the commit subject mentioning Appointment.status, the patch did not add discontinued to Appointment, which matches the final disposition.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes both Encounter and Appointment. Current Appointment.status includes fulfilled with wording that Encounter tracks further status changes and omits discontinued. Later FHIR-22726 added Encounter.discharged and fixed the discontinued definition typo without reversing FHIR-18827. PA May 2019 minutes confirm the WG decided post-fulfillment status tracking belongs on Encounter.status.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source already satisfies the issue and adding discontinued to Appointment.status would contradict the published resolution.

related_jiras.note: Appointment waitlist/fulfilled context helps explain why Appointment.status hands later status tracking to Encounter. It was not decided here because it is a separate already-applied waitlist issue.
Later Encounter status work added discharged and fixed the discontinued definition typo while preserving the FHIR-18827 semantics.
